about.cta.p1: At Manta Shark Aquatics, we make sure all students don't just learn to swim — they master the water for life. We provide your family with a
about.diff.noRelearn.text: We eliminate the frustration of half-built skills. While students have fun, the correct learning foundations are being repeatedly practiced.
about.diff.noRelearn.title: No Re-Learning Required
about.diff.patient.text: We don't believe in "quick fixes." If a skill is vital to your child's safety, we take the effort to ensure they master it completely.
about.diff.patient.title: Patient, Efficient Progression
about.diff.peace.text: With certified lifeguards, experienced instructors, and educational psychologists on the team, your child is in the safest hands.
about.diff.peace.title: Total Peace of Mind
about.diff.subtitle: What makes us different is that we focus on fundamental swim techniques from day one. Our parents stay for the long term because they value a deep, correct foundation over rushed shortcuts.
about.diff.wellbeing.text: We ensure students are healthy, learning at their own comfortable pace, and having genuine fun — turning a scary experience into a joyful routine.
about.diff.wellbeing.title: Holistic Student Wellbeing
about.hero.subtitle: Professional coaching rooted in education, psychology, sports science, and child development.
about.phil.p1a: Having a team of professionals from unique training and backgrounds, our teaching and training philosophy is like no other. When we say we are
about.phil.p1b: we mean that we take our craft of teaching seriously, and your child's learning experience, safety, and long-term development are our absolute priorities.
about.phil.p2a: As busy professional parents, your time is valuable and your child's well-being is paramount. When you join the Manta Shark family, you can
about.phil.p2b: . We handle the technique, the safety, and the motivation, making swim day a seamless, rewarding, and stress-free part of your family's routine.
about.phil.title2: One Less Thing to Worry About.
about.team.subtitle: Passionate, professional, and effective — we love seeing our students enjoy the fun of swim lessons and demonstrate improvement and progress!
about.us.p1: At Manta Shark Aquatics, we believe swimming lessons should be more than just learning how to move through the water. They should build confidence, safety, discipline, and lifelong comfort in aquatic environments.
about.us.p2: Our team combines professional swimming experience with backgrounds in education, psychology, sports science, behavioral health, and child development — from beginner swimmers to advanced athletes, we focus on structured, progression-based instruction that builds strong fundamentals correctly from day one.
about.us.p3: Parents choose Manta Shark because they know their children are learning in a safe, supportive, and highly professional environment. We aim to make every lesson productive, encouraging, and stress-free for families.

assess.after.title: You leave knowing where your child stands

assess.cta.note: Already assessed with us? Head straight to points and pricing.
assess.cta.title: Ready when you are
assess.faq.body: What to pack, the pool temperature, where you sit to watch, and what to do if your child is nervous — all answered on our questions page.
assess.faq.title: Bringing your child for the first time?
assess.hero.sub: Thirty minutes in the water with a coach, one-on-one. At the end we give your child a level, and every lesson after that is planned around it.
assess.hero.title: Every swimmer begins with an assessment
assess.ladder.caption: For example: a child who stops at Level 3 starts lessons at Level 3.
assess.ladder.stop: Not smooth yet: this is the level
assess.next.l1.body: There are seven levels, and each one is taught in three stages. Whatever stage your child is on, that is what the coach teaches.
assess.next.l1.title: Lessons match where your child is
assess.next.l2.body: Each skill is ticked off once your child can do it, so you can see how many are done and which ones are left in the current stage.
assess.next.l2.title: A progress record after every lesson
assess.next.l3.body: After each lesson the coach writes down what they saw, in your account, in English or Chinese. You do not have to rely on what your child remembers to tell you.
assess.next.l3.title: Notes from the coach
assess.next.title: The level decides what your child practices next
assess.what.body: The coach asks your child to do the Level 1 skills, then Level 2, then Level 3, and keeps going. When your child cannot do a skill yet — or can do it but not comfortably — we stop there. That is their level.
assess.what.title: We start at Level 1 and work up until we find the right place to begin
assess.what.why: Why start from the bottom? Because that way nothing gets missed and nothing gets guessed. We are not after a sense of how well your child swims. We want to know exactly which skill the next lesson should start from.

faq.a.age: Children can start from age 3. If your child has a medical condition or any needs we should know about, please tell us before the first lesson so we can plan for it.
faq.a.assessCancel: Not online. Send us a message or call, and we will cancel it for you.
faq.a.bring: A swimsuit, a towel, goggles and a swim cap — we recommend a cap for long hair. Bring drinking water or a sports drink too.
faq.a.buy: You add points to your account and book from that balance. One point is one dollar, and the Points page lists what each kind of lesson costs. Your swimmer needs a Swim Assessment before anything else can be booked.
faq.a.cancel: From your dashboard, up to 24 hours before the lesson starts. The points go straight back to your account and you can rebook whenever suits you. Rescheduling more than 24 hours ahead is unlimited, and a moved lesson is never re-priced.
faq.a.crying: Crying in the first few lessons is normal — the pool is a new place and the coach is a new person. Our coaches start with games and play, so your child gets used to them first. Once they relax, the swimming starts.
faq.a.diaper: Yes. Babies and children who are not toilet trained wear a swim diaper, with a swimsuit over it.
faq.a.duration: Private, semi-private and group lessons are 30 minutes. Two 30-minute slots back to back can be booked as one continuous 60-minute lesson, which costs exactly twice as much. Swim Team practices are 90 minutes.
faq.a.expiry: Points you buy never expire, there is no fee for holding them, and anything you have not spent can be refunded at any time for exactly what you paid. Bonus points we give you — a referral reward, for example — are different: they last one year from the day they are added, are used before your purchased points, and cannot be refunded for cash.
faq.a.late: Inside 24 hours a lesson cannot be rescheduled and the points are not returned, because the coach's time is already reserved for you. If you have a late-cancellation allowance left you can spend one and get the points back in full — you earn one for every 10 lessons your family completes, and your dashboard shows how many you have.
faq.a.levelHow: By the Swim Assessment — not by age, and not by how long they have taken lessons elsewhere. There are seven levels, each taught in three stages, and every swimmer starts a level at Stage 1.
faq.a.pair24: Not online, because a second family shares that slot. Contact us and our team will sort it out with both families.
faq.a.pairing: You choose — a sibling, or a friend at a similar level. If the second swimmer is from another family, that family needs an account with us so both of you can confirm the booking.
faq.a.pool: Indoors and heated, kept between 88°F and 92°F.
faq.a.progress: After each lesson the coach ticks off the skills your child can now do and writes you a note. Both are in your account, so you can see how many skills are done in the current stage and which ones are left.
faq.a.referral: Yes. Your referral code is in the Points section of your dashboard. When a friend enters it while registering and then takes their first paid lesson, you and your friend each receive 40 bonus points. The code has to be entered at registration, the Swim Assessment does not count, and bonus points are valid for one year and cannot be refunded for cash.
faq.a.refund: Yes, and there is no minimum — whatever is left, however small, comes back to you. Points you paid for and have not spent are refundable at any time, one dollar per point, with no deadline and no fee. Points already spent on lessons are not, and neither are points we gave you as a credit or a goodwill gesture: those can be spent on lessons but were never money. Ask us in chat or at the front desk and a team member will handle it.
faq.a.shared: Yes. The balance belongs to the family account rather than to one child, and any swimmer on the account can book from it.
faq.a.start: Every swimmer begins with a Swim Assessment — 30 minutes, one-on-one, $85, one per swimmer. The coach works up from Level 1 until they find where your child is, and that level is what every lesson after it is built around. Lessons cannot be booked until a swimmer has a level.
faq.a.teamBilling: As a monthly membership per swimmer that renews automatically until you cancel. You can cancel any time before your next billing date, and the membership stays active through the period you have already paid for.
faq.a.teamWhat: 90 minutes, up to 24 swimmers per squad, working on stroke technique, endurance, turns and race strategy.
faq.a.teamWho: Swimmers at Level 4 and above. Squads are grouped by level, so your child trains with swimmers at a similar stage.
faq.a.watch: Yes. There is seating where you can sit and watch the whole lesson.
faq.a.weather: The pool is indoors and heated, so weather almost never stops a lesson. If we ever do have to cancel — severe weather or something else outside our control — we notify you by email and SMS, and the points go straight back to your account.

levels.1.desc: A child who has never been in water, starting from "there are rules near the pool". This level teaches safety and trust, not swimming — by the end the face goes in, the body floats, and they can climb out on their own.
levels.1.goal.1: Waits for the coach at the edge, and can point out the deep end and where not to run
levels.1.goal.2: Enters feet-first on the coach's word, and climbs out unaided by the ladder or the wall
levels.1.goal.3: Puts the whole face in for three seconds, blowing bubbles through the mouth and the nose
levels.1.goal.4: Floats on the front and on the back for five seconds with one hand of support
levels.1.goal.5: Glides five yards off the wall, arms straight, doing nothing else
levels.1.tagline: Trust, comfort and safety around water.
levels.2.desc: Floating comes first, then moving: kicking, bobbing, the first crossings into deep water. The word for this level is relax — the harder they try, the more they sink. By the end they jump into deep water and come back to the wall themselves.
levels.2.goal.1: Pushes off into a front float for five seconds; holds a breath underwater for five seconds with the eyes open
levels.2.goal.2: Starfish floats on the back for ten seconds with nobody helping
levels.2.goal.3: Kicks ten yards on a board, and ten yards on the back
levels.2.goal.4: Ten bobs in chest-deep water and ten in over-head water, rhythm unbroken
levels.2.goal.5: Retrieves an object from the bottom on the first try
levels.2.goal.6: Jumps feet-first into deep water, surfaces and returns to the wall unaided
levels.2.tagline: From floating to moving, and into deep water for the first time.
levels.3.desc: The first time they get anywhere on their own. The board comes away, the breath goes in, and deep water stops being the part to avoid. The level closes with one complete water safety test — seven moves from the jump to the climb out, in a single run.
levels.3.goal.1: Kicks 25 yards on a board and 25 yards on the back, without stopping or standing up
levels.3.goal.2: Kicks ten yards with no board, lifting the head for a breath and putting the face straight back in
levels.3.goal.3: Pushes off in a tight streamline and glides seven yards before the first kick
levels.3.goal.4: Starfish floats on the back for 30 seconds in deep water, relaxed
levels.3.goal.5: Retrieves an object from the deep-water bottom and swims it back to the wall
levels.3.goal.6: Passes the water safety test: jump into deep water, retrieve the toy, five bobs, starfish float 30 seconds, kick to the mark, climb out — one unbroken run
levels.3.tagline: Moving without help, and passing the water safety test.
levels.4.desc: Real strokes begin here. Freestyle and backstroke each grow into a whole movement, and the breaststroke and butterfly kicks start laying track. Drills appear for the first time — from this level the question is not whether they finish, but whether it is right.
levels.4.goal.1: Swims 15 yards of freestyle breathing to the side, then 25 yards without stopping
levels.4.goal.2: Freestyle arms that match on both sides, the breath no longer stuck on one side, the shoulder rolling clear of the water
levels.4.goal.3: Swims 25 yards of freestyle as fast as they can with the stroke holding together
levels.4.goal.4: Swims backstroke from a single-arm drill out to 25 yards, the shoulder rolling and every stroke pressing through to the thigh
levels.4.goal.5: Breaststroke kick with its four beats kept apart — tuck, turn the feet out, push, snap together — and 10 yards of it on a board
levels.4.goal.6: Butterfly kick 25 yards on a board, the wave driven from the chest
levels.4.tagline: Where the four strokes start: freestyle and backstroke take shape.
levels.5.desc: Distances lengthen, the first flip turn arrives, and breaststroke and butterfly get their first whole movement. Each of the four strokes runs as its own line through this level, and this is where the drills are thickest — backstroke alone has three.
levels.5.goal.1: Swims 50 yards of freestyle with a turn, then 100 yards continuously
levels.5.goal.2: Completes a freestyle flip turn: both feet on the wall, pushing off in a streamline on the back
levels.5.goal.3: Swims 50 yards of backstroke, the body rolling with the arm instead of lying flat and forcing it
levels.5.goal.4: Breaststroke kick 25 yards with a glide after every kick, then ten yards of full breaststroke
levels.5.goal.5: Completes an open turn: both hands on the wall together, then turn and push off
levels.5.goal.6: The first step into butterfly — finding the two-kicks-to-a-pull rhythm, one arm carrying all the way through
levels.5.tagline: Longer swims, the first turns, breaststroke and butterfly taking shape.
levels.6.desc: Butterfly and breaststroke become real strokes here and all four are on the board — the watershed of the whole programme, the level after which a child says they can swim. Freestyle stretches to 200 yards, the flip turn arrives, and butterfly and breaststroke each go out to 50, which is the runway into the last level.
levels.6.goal.1: Dolphin kicks 15 yards underwater on one breath off the wall
levels.6.goal.2: Swims 200 yards of freestyle with turns, every 50 within five seconds of the last
levels.6.goal.3: Swims 100 yards of backstroke with turns, and completes a legal backstroke flip turn
levels.6.goal.4: Swims butterfly from 10 yards out to 50, two kicks to a pull all the way to the wall
levels.6.goal.5: Swims breaststroke from 15 yards out to 50, and completes two breaststroke drills
levels.6.goal.6: Kicks 25 yards of each stroke in medley order with no rest between them
levels.6.tagline: All four strokes, plus endurance and turns.
levels.7.desc: Fifty yards in each of the four strokes first, then a hundred in each, legal and inside the time band the programme sets. There is one band per distance — no split by sex, none by age. What matters is the comparison with last month, not with the swimmer in the next lane. Our pool does not do dive starts, so every swim is timed from a push start.
levels.7.goal.1: Swims 50 and 100 yards of freestyle inside the time band, legally
levels.7.goal.2: Swims 50 and 100 yards of backstroke inside the time band
levels.7.goal.3: Swims 50 and 100 yards of breaststroke inside the time band, with a legal pullout
levels.7.goal.4: Swims 50 and 100 yards of butterfly inside the time band, the rhythm holding on the second length
levels.7.goal.5: Swims 500 yards of freestyle, holding their own pace across every 50
levels.7.goal.6: Transitions and turns all legal, finishing a 100 yard individual medley
levels.7.tagline: The four strokes at 50 and 100 on the clock, then the medley.

mastery.def.1: Willing to try, but the movement is wrong and it needs constant prompting or a hand.
mastery.def.2: The movement is right, but a hand or a cue is still needed to finish it.
mastery.def.3: Nobody touching, nobody prompting, and it gets done once. Not necessarily pretty, not necessarily every time.
mastery.def.4: Two or three in a row, with only small faults left.
mastery.def.5: Matches the pass criteria above, and still there at the next lesson.
mastery.hint: Reaching "On their own" is enough to start the next skill. "Mastered" passes this one.
